title: A nonstandard fractional Jacobi pseudospectral method for weakly regular right-sided Caputo terminal problems
comment: Subitted to Applied Mathematics and Computation 8th January 2026
summary: Right-sided fractional differential equations arising in terminal value problems present substantial analytical and numerical challenges due to their intrinsic nonlocal structure and the presence of weak algebraic-type singularities near the terminal point. These singular behaviors significantly degrade the performance of classical finite-difference, finite-element, and standard spectral methods, which typically rely on smoothness assumptions that break down in the fractional setting. In this work, we develop a comprehensive fractional pseudospectral framework specifically designed for nonlinear right-sided Caputo terminal value systems. The proposed method employs a versatile family of nonstandard fractional Jacobi basis functions whose endpoint-weighted structure naturally reflects the asymptotic behavior of right-sided fractional operators. This construction enables the accurate approximation of solutions with limited regularity near the terminal point, without requiring smoothing transformations or mesh grading. We establish the existence and uniqueness of the discrete numerical solution and derive rigorous convergence estimates that faithfully capture the inherent singularity structure of the problem. A series of numerical experiments validates the theoretical developments and demonstrates that the proposed approach delivers high-order accuracy and superior resolution of terminal-layer behavior compared with traditional spectral techniques. The resulting framework provides an efficient and reliable computational tool for challenging nonlinear fractional terminal value systems characterized by weak solution regularity.

title: A Coupled Fluid Naghdi Shell Windkessel Model for Pulmonary Artery Banding: Partitioned Numerical Scheme and Parameter Estimation
summary:
We develop a 3D fluid structure interaction model for blood flow through deformable vessels with localized constrictions, motivated by pulmonary artery banding in neonates with congenital heart disease. The model couples incompressible Navier Stokes equations in an Arbitrary Lagrangian Eulerian framework with a Naghdi shell model for the arterial wall and a three element Windkessel model for downstream circulation. The shell describes a 3D cylindrical vessel wall with variable radius and is defined on a 2D reference domain. Its low regularity formulation retains membrane, bending, and transverse shear deformation while requiring only first derivatives of the reference midsurface, accommodating piecewise smooth geometries with discontinuous surface slopes.
  We derive the coupled variational formulation and develop a non-iterative partitioned scheme with a Robin-type interface condition incorporating arterial wall inertia. For a linearized fixed domain problem, we establish a discrete energy estimate under suitable assumptions. A unscented Kalman filter estimates proximal and distal resistances and compliance from inlet-pressure observations. Numerical experiments demonstrate consistent pressure wave propagation and wall deformation under spatial and temporal refinement. Comparisons of the standard Naghdi shell and a modified, predominantly radial shell model reveal how structural deformation mechanisms affect wave speed and displacement. An idealized pulmonary artery banding example demonstrates the coupled fluid shell Windkessel model with parameter estimation. The framework enables investigation of the hemodynamic and mechanical effects of localized constrictions and their dependence on downstream vascular properties.

title: Galerkin finite element method for time fractional diffusion-wave equations with constant time delay
summary: This paper studies numerical methods for the time fractional diffusion-wave equations with the constant delay. Using a symmetric fractional-order reduction technique and introducing the auxiliary variable $w$, we reformulate the original problem as an equivalent coupled system and for the first time carry out a rigorous regularity analysis of $w$. Based on the symmetric graded time mesh, the coupled problem is discretised by the $L1$ scheme in time and a standard finite element method in space, and the stability result of the developed fully discrete finite element scheme is established by means of a discrete fractional Grönwall inequality. Furthermore, we derive a new comparison principle and reconstruct a new barrier function on each interval $((k-1)τ,kτ]$, $1\le k\le K$ according to the properties of the symmetric graded mesh. Based on the new barrier function, we obtain new relevant properties, which lead to a novel and crucial stability property for the discrete fractional operator. Combining the obtained local truncation error in time gives a local error estimate for the fully discrete finite element scheme, which shows that our convergence result provides a unified framework that seamlessly encompasses both pointwise-in-time error estimates on uniform meshes and global-in-time error estimates on symmetrical graded meshes. Numerical experiments confirm the theoretical results.

title: Adaptive Randomized Neural Networks for PDEs: Structure-Aware Feature Redistribution and Residual-Driven Block Enrichment
summary: Randomized neural networks retain an output-linear least-squares solve, but globally sampled random features may fail to capture the spatial and scale structure of PDE solutions. We propose SFRBE--RaNN, a two-stage adaptive trial-space construction. SFR redistributes a fixed feature budget according to regional indicator masses and adapts regional weight scales through low-dimensional residual-based optimization. RBE constructs nonredundant enrichments by screening multiple activation families, removing represented response directions, and selecting the smallest admissible prefix. For solution-dependent operators, candidates are screened with a frozen operator and accepted only after nonlinear residual verification. For fixed linear problems, we establish an exact discrete residual-reduction identity and a conditional solution-error estimate. Building on this identity, we combine safeguarded SFR with RBE capture factors to derive a finite-horizon error bound involving baseline best approximation and empirical consistency, together with a conditional random-search success-probability bound. Numerical experiments on localized, multiscale, and nonlinear space--time problems demonstrate the method's effectiveness.

title: Transport in multilayer graphene: resistance from stacking faults
comment: 15 pages, 6 figures. Submitted to Physical Review X
summary: Multilayer graphene exhibits rich possibilities for stacking. While natural bulk graphite predominantly occurs in the Bernal structure, where layers are stacked in an $-ABAB-$ pattern, rhombohedral stacking has sprung to prominence recently. It is well known that Bernal graphite exhibits anisotropic transport, with high resistance to currents along the stacking axis. Careful experiments using pillar geometries have measured out-of-plane resistance, attributing it to stacking faults where planes slip out of the nominal $ABAB$ sequence. The observed resistance shows anomalously large, non-Gaussian, sample-to-sample variations. In this article, we build a theoretical framework to calculate $c$-axis resistance of graphene stacks with an arbitrary stacking arrangement. Our approach builds on the idea that, regardless of stacking sequence, we have in-plane translational symmetry. With in-plane momentum as a good quantum number, $c$-axis transport reduces to an effectively one-dimensional problem that can be addressed using the Landauer paradigm. We calculate the resistances of a variety of simple stacking faults in both Bernal and rhombohedral systems. We also calculate the resistance of a rhombohedral 'slab' embedded between Bernal leads. Remarkably, despite both Bernal and rhombohedral graphite being metallic, the system exhibits insulating behaviour. We attribute this to Fermi surface mismatch. We next calculate the resistance of a multilayer sample with stacking disorder. Resistance is non-self-averaging, akin to a one-dimensional wire where disorder has a strong localizing effect. The median resistance grows exponentially with stack size, indicating insulating character driven by localization. Our results demonstrate that transport measurements on mesoscopic graphitic pillars serve as signatures of stacking faults, and in particular, probe localization-driven physics.

title: Equality of the Jellium and the Uniform Electron Gas Energies
comment: GitHub repo with Lean formalization: https://github.com/xyzw/jellium_ueg
summary: Jellium, a system of electrons in a uniform neutralizing background, and the uniform electron gas (UEG), a system of electrons with constant density and no background, are two standard models of the electron gas. We prove that the ground-state energy per unit volume of Jellium, as defined by Lieb and Narnhofer, coincides with the UEG energy defined by Lewin, Lieb and Seiringer, i.e. \[ e^\hbar_{\rm Jel}(ρ_0)=e^\hbar_{\rm UEG}(ρ_0). \] This equality was previously established in the classical case by Lewin, Lieb and Seiringer and independently by Cotar and Petrache.

title: A geometric criterion for the dimension of Morgan-Scott spline spaces $S_{2r}^r(Δ_{\mathrm{MS}})$
summary: We establish a geometric dimension criterion for spline spaces on nondegenerate standard Morgan-Scott triangulations with four distinct edge directions at each interior vertex. For every integer $r\ge1$, concurrence of the three auxiliary lines joining corresponding interior and boundary vertices implies that $\dim S_{2r}^r(Δ_{\mathrm{MS}})$ exceeds the Schumaker lower bound by one. The proof constructs a quadratic form through the six dual spoke points and uses its $r$th power to define a nonzero functional annihilating the image of the smoothing-cofactor map. Diener's upper bound then gives the dimension formula. We also give a matrix representation of this functional and an explicit example in the quadratic case. Combined with the known necessary conditions and the negative-branch exclusion of Deng, Feng, and Kozak, the result yields a necessary and sufficient concurrence criterion for $r>2$.

title: Resonant enhancement of Raman scattering in a MoS$_2$ nanotube
summary: The whispering-gallery modes confined in the wall of a multiwall MoS$_2$ nanotube resonantly enhance the spontaneous Raman scattering by its own optical phonons. The enhancement is doubly resonant --- pump and Stokes waves hit two adjacent modes at one pump energy, and the signal scales as $(Q_{\rm pump}Q_{\rm sc})^2$ - whenever a phonon energy matches the free spectral range of the mode ladder. Near the A exciton the excitonic dispersion compresses the ladder and sweeps its spacing through all intralayer phonon energies of MoS$_2$, so the match, reached for $A_{1g}$ at $E_{\rm pump}=1551$~meV, requires no geometric tuning. A missed match splits the excitation peak into a pump- and a scattered-resonant doublet whose splitting measures the residual detuning. Selection rules confine the double resonance to the TM$\to$TM channel and exclude $E_{1g}$.

title: Free Fermion frustration-free models have zero Hall conductance
summary: We give a new proof that translation-invariant free Fermion frustration-free models have zero Hall conductance. Our proof is analytic in nature and it uses the bulk-edge correspondence. The central argument, which holds beyond the translation-invariant situation, is that in frustration-free models, edge modes cannot merge into the ground state band. We give an example of a gapped frustration-free model that is nonetheless gapless on the half-plane.

title: A Hybrid High-Order method for variable-exponent Leray-Lions problems with convergence under minimal regularity
summary: We consider a homogeneous Dirichlet problem for nonlinear elliptic equations in divergence form with Leray--Lions fluxes of variable growth. The class includes the variable-exponent $p(\cdot)$-Laplacian and regularized Carreau--Yasuda-type laws. We propose and analyze a Hybrid High-Order (HHO) discretization on general polytopal meshes, a hybrid nonconforming method based on cell and face polynomial unknowns of arbitrary degree. We develop a variable-exponent polynomial and discrete functional toolkit centered on a mean-exponent norm equivalence, together with inverse, trace, Poincaré--Wirtinger, Sobolev--Poincaré, discrete Lebesgue embedding, interpolation, and compactness estimates adapted to HHO unknowns. We then establish well-posedness of the nonlinear discrete problem and convergence without assuming additional regularity of the exact solution beyond its natural energy space. The discrete potential converges strongly in every uniformly subcritical variable-exponent Lebesgue space, the reconstructed gradient converges strongly in the natural variable-exponent space, and the stabilization energy vanishes. Numerical experiments in two, three, and four space dimensions confirm convergence for singular solutions and for exponent fields ranging from close to $1$ up to $6$. Quantitative a priori error estimates for the same method are derived in a companion paper.

title: One-way electron mirrors from single-layer stacking shifts in rhombohedral graphite
summary: One-way mirrors or asymmetric scatterers are key components of photonic systems, protecting sources from back-reflections and routing light along a chosen path. Acoustic systems can also be engineered to show asymmetric reflection. However, a condensed matter platform acting as a one-way mirror without breaking linearity, time-reversal symmetry or energy conservation has been lacking. One route to achieving this is mode selection, where a probe coupled to only some modes sees a boundary as a mirror from one side and as transparent from the other. Here we show that single-layer stacking shifts in six-layer rhombohedral graphite provide this platform, acting as one-way mirrors for electrons. In scanning tunneling microscopy, 10 nm scale interference fringes appear only on the stacking fault side of a wall, tracking its Dirac band, the rhombohedral side remaining transparent. Layer-resolved tight-binding and wave-packet dynamics calculations reproduce this and trace the asymmetry to the mismatched layer polarization across the wall, with the tip supplying the selective coupling. Because stacking solitons glide under external fields, this mirror forms a movable element of electron optics defined by the crystal structure alone.

title: Poisson statistics for one-dimensional Anderson--Bernoulli Schrödinger operators
summary: We prove Poisson local eigenvalue statistics for one-dimensional Schrödinger operators with nondegenerate Bernoulli potentials at any fixed nonzero coupling. After unfolding by the integrated density of states (IDS), the local eigenvalue process converges to a Poisson point process of unit intensity at every energy in the interior of the almost-sure spectrum. The theorem also holds for bounded nonconstant iid potentials, provided the IDS is continuous and strictly increasing near the reference energy. If the IDS also has a finite positive derivative at that energy, the usual linear normalization gives the same limit. The proof uses a phase coordinate with exact IDS drift to obtain a uniform exponential crossing law and joint Poisson counts in disjoint energy windows.

title: On the stability of basis construction in extended Krylov subspace methods
summary: Extended Krylov subspace methods (EKSMs) are a well known approach for approximating the action of a matrix function on a vector $f(A)\mathbf{b}$, and their block versions are often used for solving Lyapunov and Sylvester matrix equations. EKSMs produce Laurent approximations to the underlying operator, which are generally more accurate per iteration than polynomial KSMs, without requiring a pole selection procedure as rational KSMs do. At the same time, due to the expansion of the search space by not only $A$ but also by its inverse, a number of implementation choices must be made that can affect the stability of the algorithm in floating-point arithmetic. We concentrate on two variants that often appear in the literature and in code, based on whether new basis vectors are built via what we denote as ``mixed channels" or ``split channels." We characterize their loss of orthogonality with an easily computable metric and prove that when $A$ is symmetric positive definite, mixed channels have better orthogonality than split channels; however, numerical experiments demonstrate that straightforward predictions are not possible for indefinite or nonsymmetric matrices. We also provide a modular MATLAB toolbox, \texttt{ektoolbox}, that contains new versions of EKSMs with low-synchronization Gram-Schmidt backbones.

title: Transdimensional Chern insulators in rhombohedral multilayer graphene superlattices
comment: 5 pages, 4 figures; Supplementary Material: 17 pages, 4 figures
summary: Recent experiments on lightly electron-doped rhombohedral multilayer graphene (RMG) in the "transdimensional" regime revealed anomalous Hall hysteresis under both perpendicular and in-plane magnetic fields, pointing to the emergence of transdimensional orbital magnetism in an interaction-driven "Fermi-lune" metal. Here we demonstrate that, by coupling to the moiré potential, this transdimensional orbital ferromagnetic metal can evolve into quantized Chern insulator phases in twisted RMG/hBN moiré superlattices. Using unrestricted Hartree-Fock calculations, we find that interaction-driven reconstruction isolates a spin-valley-polarized $|C| = 1$ Chern band, leading to a "transdimensional Chern insulator" (TDCI) state exhibiting both in-plane and out-of-plane orbital magnetizations. A minimal two-band model is introduced to describe the unique properties of TDCI, which unveils the intimate connection between non-reciprocal velocity and in-plane orbital magnetization. We further analyze the collective excitations of TDCIs, and identify soft charge and spin modes that may lead to density wave instabilities in certain cases. An in-plane magnetic field can harden the soft density-wave mode and may drive a transition from density-wave state to TDCI. Finally, when the $|C| = 1$ band is fractionally filled, the many-body ground state may be a fractional Chern insulator with broken rotation and mirror symmetries.

title: Semiclassical Band Splitting in the Infinite Chern Band Model
summary: We study the two lowest Bloch bands of the infinite Chern band model in the semiclassical limit. When the Berry curvature parameter is an odd multiple of \(π\), we derive an explicit asymptotic formula for their exponentially small splitting, uniformly over the Brillouin torus. The proof combines Agmon estimates and WKB approximations for a matrix Schrödinger operator whose lowest potential eigenvalue has two wells. Geometric properties of the Agmon distance allow us to compute the leading tunneling coefficients by the method of stationary phase. We provide numerical computations to illustrate the asymptotic formula and support the conjecture that the two bands remain separated for other values of the Berry curvature parameter.

title: A priori error estimates for a Hybrid High-Order method on variable-exponent Leray-Lions problems
summary: We derive a priori error estimates for the Hybrid High-Order (HHO) discretization of variable-exponent Leray--Lions problems introduced in a companion convergence study. HHO methods belong to the family of hybrid nonconforming methods, based on cell and face polynomial unknowns of arbitrary degree. Under additional broken regularity of the exact solution and its flux, we establish a localized error estimate that retains the individual element sizes and a global estimate whose rate distinguishes the purely subquadratic, mixed subquadratic--superquadratic, and purely superquadratic regimes. In the subquadratic range, we also derive a regime-dependent refinement that compares the local approximation scale with the local non-degeneracy scale and recovers the optimal polynomial order when that scale is resolved by the mesh. The analysis relies on variable-exponent approximation properties of polynomial projectors, mean-exponent tools for discrete polynomial spaces, and weighted monotonicity estimates. The framework also covers regularized and mildly non-symmetric anisotropic Carreau--Yasuda-type fluxes. Numerical experiments on Cartesian and Voronoi meshes support the predicted rates and show that the regularity assumption on the flux cannot be dispensed with.

title: Edge state reconstruction in proximitized graphene and its probe using RKKY interaction
comment: 10 pages and 38 Figures. Comments are welcome
summary: Proximity induced spin-orbit coupling (SOC) in graphene emerges when it is placed on a substrate, breaking sublattice symmetry and giving rise to staggered intrinsic SOC together with Rashba spin-orbit coupling. In zigzag graphene nanoribbons, this staggered SOC produces pseudohelical edge states exhibiting sublattice-locked rather than spin-locked helicity. We investigate the effect of a finite on-site potential, restricted to the edges of the ribbon, on these edge states. We find the inter-valley edge states undergo reconstruction and become purely intra-valley, exhibiting both spin and valley polarization. The charge conductance calculations fail to capture this reconstruction, since the number of transmitted channels remains unchanged. We show that the Ruderman-Kittel-Kasuya-Yosida (RKKY) magnetic exchange interaction, between two magnetic impurities situated on the ribbon edge can be used to probe the shifted band dispersion, for both the uniform and staggered spin-orbit coupling. In the presence of strong intrinsic and Rashba SOC, the RKKY interaction becomes fully anisotropic. Both sublattice staggering and edge potential-induced reconstruction lead to distinct features in the RKKY interaction. We show that the RKKY interaction terms acquire faster oscillations as a function of the spatial separation between two magnetic impurities, in response to the edge state reconstruction, establishing it as an effective probe of the edge states. Additionally, the significant mismatch in the amplitudes of the DM term corresponding to the uniform and staggered SOC, can also act as a probe of the type of SOC.

title: Approach to Equilibrium in Translation-Invariant Quantum Systems: Structural Results II
summary:
We continue the development, started in [AHP 25 (2023), 715-749], of a structural theory of approach to equilibrium in translation-invariant quantum spin systems. Dynamical Steady States (DSS) are defined as w*-limit points of the time-averaged evolution of an initial state. We show that if a DSS is an equilibrium state of a sufficiently regular interaction, then the specific energy of this interaction is necessarily a constant of the motion. Two distinct mechanisms lead to this conclusion, one based on dynamical surface energies and the other on conservation of specific relative entropy. We conjecture that these properties hold for a natural class of interactions.
  For a DSS admitting a physical equilibrium description, the associated equilibrium states are characterized by a dynamical Gibbs variational principle: they are precisely the minimizers of the specific relative entropy from the initial state over the physical equilibrium states. The achieved minimum equals the increase of specific entropy.
  The structural theory also yields characterizations of approach to thermal equilibrium, based on two model-dependent questions: restoration of a sufficiently local thermodynamic description at large times and classification of the corresponding local constants of motion. Once locality is restored, the constants of motion determine the possible asymptotic equilibrium states. In particular, if finite-range locality is restored and the energy is the only finite-range constant of the motion, then every DSS is a thermal equilibrium state at the temperature fixed by energy conservation. The finite-time dynamical input underlying this theory is established in a companion paper.

title: Greedy multiscale kernel algorithms
summary: Multiscale kernel approximation and greedy kernel algorithms are two established tools for scattered data approximation. We combine them into greedy multiscale kernel algorithms, in which every level of a multiscale residual correction is constructed by a greedy kernel algorithm. For the multiscale $f$-greedy algorithm we prove convergence rates in the number of selected centres which coincide (up to an arbitrarily small loss in the exponent) with the rates of the single-scale $f$-greedy algorithm. The gain of the multiscale construction is in the stability, and we make this precise by a two-sided estimate for the condition number of kernel matrices with rescaled kernels. The lower bound shows that any single-scale method, and in particular the $f$-greedy algorithm, pays for its convergence rate with condition numbers growing at least like a power of the number of centres. In contrast, the multiscale scaling of the kernel keeps this lower bound fixed on every level without changing the rate. The upper bound identifies the separation of the centres at the scale of the kernel as the quantity to control. We give the operation counts of all the methods considered and compare the greedy multiscale algorithms numerically with single-scale greedy and classical multiscale methods, in terms of error, time and conditioning.

title: Imaging defects in two-dimensional crystals by convergent beam electron diffraction
summary: Convergent beam electron diffraction (CBED), recently demonstrated on two-dimensional (2D) materials, offers a number of interesting applications such as imaging atomic in- and out-of plane shifts, interlayer distances, and individual adsorbates. In this study, we show how CBED allows for atomic-precision imaging of individual defects in 2D materials using one single-shot intensity measurement. In combination with structural calculations using density functional theory, we present simulated CBED patterns for various defects in graphene, each of which exhibits a unique fingerprint distribution. We also show how atomic positions, including the individual atomic defects in graphene, can be reconstructed by iterative phase retrieval from a single CBED pattern.

title: Dynamical Conservation Laws in Quantum Spin Systems
summary: We study dynamical conservation laws and the propagation of thermodynamic structure in translation-invariant lattice quantum spin systems. Using Lieb-Robinson bounds [CMP 28 (1972), 251-257] in arbitrary dimension, and Araki's bounds [CMP 14 (1969), 120-157] in dimension one, we prove conservation of the specific entropy, specific energy, and specific relative entropy under suitable assumptions on the interactions. The transported local Hamiltonians admit surface energies that vanish per unit volume in the van Hove limit, and local observables remain a core for the transported generators at every finite time. Weak Gibbsianity is preserved for sufficiently small times in arbitrary dimension and for all times in dimension one. These results provide the analytical foundation for the structural theory of approach to equilibrium developed in a companion paper, and establish partial results toward the conjectures formulated there.

title: Projection-Based Parareal for Nonlinear Initial-Value Problems
summary: Parareal is a parallel-in-time method for initial-value problems that has found extensive applications and given rise to many variants. Krylov-enhanced parareal is a variant of parareal that uses projection techniques to accelerate convergence substantially for linear problems. In this paper, we study a projection-based parareal algorithm for nonlinear initial-value problems with a modified iteration scheme and an arbitrary orthogonal projection. For a general nonlinear problem, we prove a convergence estimate for each iteration step on a fixed time grid. We analyze the errors of the modified scheme and the scheme of Krylov-enhanced parareal relative to the old error as the coarse grid is refined. For a coarse solver of order $p$ and step size $h$, we prove error bounds of $O(h^{p+1})$ for the modified scheme and $O(h)$ for that of Krylov-enhanced parareal at the first potentially inexact time point under mild assumptions. Numerical experiments on two nonlinear problems are consistent with the theoretical analysis.

title: Theory of Dispersion and Exchange Interactions Subjected to Surface Roughness in Application to Signal Transmission through a Nanoswitch
summary: We present the theoretical description of a resistive nanoswitch designated for a change-over between the two operation modes by calculating the electri elastic, dispersion (van der Waals and Casimir), and also exchange repulsive forces in its configuration with an account of surface roughness. The dispersion forces are described by means of the Lifshitz theory and, at the shortest separations between the interacting bodies, where this theory is inapplicable, by the method of additive summation of the interatomic potentials corrected for the role of the effects of nonadditivity. The exchange repulsion is also found by a summation of the interatomic potentials and using the proximity force approximation. It is shown that the nanoswitch possesses the equilibrium closest separation between a cantilever tip and a ground plate calculated as a function of the actuation voltage and operates in a cyclic manner with no pull-in when this voltage is switched on and off. We have found the tunnel current between a cantilever tip and a plate and investigated distortions appearing in the signal transmitted through a nanoswitch. According to our results, the amplitude distortions arising in the low-frequency information signal can be made sufficiently small by increasing a difference between the amplitudes of the carrier and information signals. Possible applications of the obtained results are discussed.

title: Augmentation curve for torus knots
summary: We prove a version of topological recursion for the correlation differentials of colored HOMFLY-PT polynomials of torus knots on the corresponding augmentation curves, following the proposal of Gu, Jockers, Klemm, and Soroush. To this end, we explicitly construct the spectral curve from the so-called auxiliary curve of Brini, Eynard, and Mariño and prove that it coincides with the augmentation curve for every torus knot with coprime $(r,s)$. Finally, our version of topological recursion proves the higher-genus closed-string prediction of the Aganagic--Vafa conjecture for all torus knot augmentation curves.

title: The $L\log L$-Luxemburg Discrepancy for Nonnegative Weights Suffers from the Curse of Dimensionality
summary: We study the normalized discrepancy in the Luxemburg norm generated by $Φ(s)=s\log(1+s)$. For arbitrary nonnegative quadrature weights, we prove that the associated information complexity suffers from the curse of dimensionality: for every $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, there exist constants $c_\varepsilon>0$ and $d_0=d_0(\varepsilon)\in\mathbb{N}$ such that \[N_{Φ,+}(\varepsilon,d)\ge c_{\varepsilon} d^{-1}(1.07735\ldots)^d \qquad \mbox{for all } d\ge d_0. \] The result therefore also applies to equal-weight quasi-Monte Carlo rules.

title: Indirect Control of Buried CoB Spin Textures via C$_{60}$-Induced Modification of Ir Spin-Orbit Coupling
summary: Understanding how organic materials modulate magnetic structure is a central challenge in organic spintronics. Here, we demonstrate that C$_{60}$ molecular films exert a pronounced and quantifiable influence on the buried magnetic spin texture in Pt/CoB/Ir based multilayer systems hosting interfacial Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction (iDMI). Using Lorentz transmission electron microscopy, the magnetic domain behaviour in field-free and in-situ field environments is measured. In Fresnel mode, we reveal a reduction in magnetic domain periodicity upon C$_{60}$ deposition. Then, using pixelated 4D-STEM differential phase contrast mode, we establish that this modification arises from a substantial enhancement of effective magnetic anisotropy and interfacial DMI strength. Coupled with bulk magnetometry and micromagnetic simulations, we propose a mechanism based on spin-orbit coupling at the C$_{60}$/Ir interface which modifies the iDMI and drives a contraction of spin texture density throughout the multilayer stack. These findings extend the impact of organic molecular capping films as effective and accessible routes for engineering spin textures to buried magnetic multilayer systems, with direct implications for the design of next-generation spintronic and neuromorphic devices.

title: On the exact quantization of BCOV Theory on Calabi-Yau Manifolds
summary: We announce the solution of constructing perturbative quantum BCOV invariants on arbitrary Calabi-Yau manifolds. In this note, we outline the construction and present an explicit solution. The quantization includes all descendant fields and all loop orders, and expresses the quantum BCOV interaction by an explicit integration over the moduli space of marked Riemann surfaces. This canonical solution provides a mathematical construction of all higher genus BCOV invariants on compact Calabi-Yau manifolds, which are conjecturally equivalent to all higher genus Gromov-Witten invariants on the mirror.

title: Stability analysis of the steady solution for incompressible lid-driven cavity flow
summary: Steady solutions at high Reynolds numbers are computed using an iterative method that linearizes the nonlinear convective terms. This linearization reduces the original nonlinear boundary-value problem to a sequence of linear problems, one solved at each iteration, thereby improving the numerical robustness of the algorithm and enabling convergence over a wide range of governing parameters. The stability of steady incompressible fluid flows is studied within the framework of a linear problem for perturbations. The original steady velocity and pressure fields are subjected to small perturbations, after which the equations are linearized with respect to the perturbations. The resulting linear problem allows one to analyze the evolution of small perturbations and to establish whether the steady solutions under consideration are stable with respect to infinitesimal perturbations. In this work, the computational implementation is based on spatial discretization by the finite element method on triangular meshes. The stability of the obtained solutions is analyzed by solving a generalized algebraic eigenvalue problem formed after discretization of the linear problem for perturbations. The presence of eigenvalues with positive real part indicates instability, whereas their absence indicates stability. Calculations were performed on a sequence of refined meshes at various Reynolds numbers for the flow in a square cavity.

title: Microwave spectroscopic evidence of a moiré-commensurate electron crystal in monolayer graphene
summary: We probe the conductivity of the lowest Landau level of a moiré-aligned monolayer graphene device by broadband microwave transmission through a coplanar waveguide ($\sim$50 mK, 15.4--18 T), isolating the longitudinal channel through a low-minus-high frequency band difference $D(ν)$. We resolve a series of minima in $D(ν)$ that drift with field along lines of fixed carrier density rather than fixed Landau filling, the hallmark of moiré-commensurate electron crystals. The strongest minimum is present at every field and matches no fractional quantum Hall or integer Hofstadter state. It lies at band filling $s=1/3$, one electron for every three moiré cells---the generalized Wigner crystal that DaSilva, Jung, and MacDonald predict as the most favorable fixed-density ($t=0$) commensuration. The weaker minima fall near neighboring commensurate fillings.

title: Fixed-Point Abundances and the Onset of Extinctions in Multispecies Lotka-Volterra Ecosystems
summary: I investigate the average and variance of species abundance distributions for fixed-point solutions to generalized Lotka-Volterra ecosystems. Two different analytical methods are constructed. First, I build up on the perturbative Random Matrix Theory approach developed in my earlier work [Phys. Rev. E. 113, L062202 (2026)], and formalize this method diagrammatically. The abundance average is given by a sum of planar diagrams with non-crossing vertex pairings which can be encoded as Dyck paths. This allows me to express the combinatorial factor multiplying perturbative terms at each order as Catalan and Narayana numbers, following which the abundance average is given by the latter's generating functions. In this way, the infinite perturbation expansion is exactly resummed in a closed-form formula. I have not been able to find a similar resummation for the abundance variance, however diagrammatic Feynman rules are expressed, following which the perturbative series can be calculated to any desirable order. Second, I do the same calculations using the cavity method, which gives closed-form formulas for both the abundance average and variance. For the average, the cavity formula gives the exact same result as the perturbative approach when the average interspecies interaction vanishes. When this is not the case, the two results are functionally different, however they are hardly distinguishable in their parametric range of validity. Comparison with numerical data indicate that the cavity result is more accurate over a larger parameter range.

title: An IMEX multi-level domain-decomposition method for the Boltzmann equation on unstructured meshes
summary: We introduce a dynamically adaptive multi-level method for the multiscale Boltzmann equation on unstructured meshes, coupling the compressible Euler, Navier-Stokes, and full Boltzmann descriptions within a single asymptotic-preserving IMEX framework. Unlike standard domain-decomposition approaches, where independent solvers exchange data only through interface conditions, the three models form a unified multiregime scheme. They share the same globally stiffly accurate IMEX Runge-Kutta discretization and are synchronized at every internal stage through kinetic-to-fluid moment projections and fluid-to-kinetic lifting. This stage-wise coupling maintains temporal consistency across model interfaces, while the asymptotic-preserving structure ensures compatibility with the fluid limit as the Knudsen number becomes small. The active description is selected in each cell through moment-realizability indicators derived from successive Chapman-Enskog approximations. The hierarchy uses Euler in near-equilibrium regions, Navier-Stokes where first-order nonequilibrium corrections are sufficient, and the full Boltzmann equation where a kinetic description is required. Using Navier-Stokes as the intermediate level avoids evolving a velocity distribution in mildly nonequilibrium regions, which is particularly advantageous on unstructured meshes, where kinetic transport dominates the cost. The spatial discretization combines finite-volume WENO reconstruction on triangular meshes with a conservative fast spectral method for the Boltzmann collision operator. Numerical experiments show that the method closely reproduces the full Boltzmann reference while significantly reducing the computational cost. These results suggest that tightly coupled AP model hierarchies are a viable alternative to interface-based domain decomposition for deterministic kinetic simulations in complex geometries.

title: Exciton superfluidity in two-dimensional bilayers at zero and high magnetic fields
summary: We study interlayer exciton superfluidity versus layer separation in two-dimensional electron-hole bilayers at zero magnetic field and quantum Hall bilayers at total filling $ν_T=1$. Unscreened Hartree-Fock theory predicts coherence at every finite separation, with an energy scale decaying inversely with separation at large distances. We examine how screening, correlations, and spatial instabilities modify this prediction. At zero field, we solve the linearized gap equation with the full momentum and frequency dependence of the interaction screened within the random-phase approximation, without an imposed cutoff. The apparent plasmon enhancement of pairing in the ladder approximation is largely cancelled by the second-order crossed-rung correction. Static screening determines the leading pairing exponent in the controlled high-density limit at fixed separation. At large separation, the pairing scale falls exponentially with squared separation while the instability persists. Extending this result to fixed density assumes Fermi-liquid layers and higher-order dynamical corrections subleading to the static pairing interaction. At high field, we obtain an analytic uniform Hartree-Fock saddle point in the lowest Landau level, coherent at every finite separation. Within Hartree-Fock theory, its finite-wave-vector collective-mode instability favors an excitonic supersolid, distinguishing loss of spatial uniformity from loss of coherence. We conjecture that the quantum Hall bilayer evolves continuously toward weak pairing of composite fermions, with a scale far below the mean-field prediction at large separation. This suppression could produce an apparent critical separation at finite temperature without a ground-state quantum phase transition. The comparison separates the existence, energy scale, and spatial stability of interlayer coherence.

title: A Coupled Fluid Naghdi Shell Windkessel Model for Pulmonary Artery Banding: Partitioned Numerical Scheme and Parameter Estimation
summary:
We develop a 3D fluid structure interaction model for blood flow through deformable vessels with localized constrictions, motivated by pulmonary artery banding in neonates with congenital heart disease. The model couples incompressible Navier Stokes equations in an Arbitrary Lagrangian Eulerian framework with a Naghdi shell model for the arterial wall and a three element Windkessel model for downstream circulation. The shell describes a 3D cylindrical vessel wall with variable radius and is defined on a 2D reference domain. Its low regularity formulation retains membrane, bending, and transverse shear deformation while requiring only first derivatives of the reference midsurface, accommodating piecewise smooth geometries with discontinuous surface slopes.
  We derive the coupled variational formulation and develop a non-iterative partitioned scheme with a Robin-type interface condition incorporating arterial wall inertia. For a linearized fixed domain problem, we establish a discrete energy estimate under suitable assumptions. A unscented Kalman filter estimates proximal and distal resistances and compliance from inlet-pressure observations. Numerical experiments demonstrate consistent pressure wave propagation and wall deformation under spatial and temporal refinement. Comparisons of the standard Naghdi shell and a modified, predominantly radial shell model reveal how structural deformation mechanisms affect wave speed and displacement. An idealized pulmonary artery banding example demonstrates the coupled fluid shell Windkessel model with parameter estimation. The framework enables investigation of the hemodynamic and mechanical effects of localized constrictions and their dependence on downstream vascular properties.

title: High-order positivity-preserving well-balanced schemes: combining flux globalization with modified Patankar deferred correction methods
summary: Positivity-preserving schemes for hyperbolic balance laws are typically built from the Zhang-Shu limiter and strong-stability-preserving Runge-Kutta (SSP-RK) time stepping, at the cost of a restrictive time-step condition. The modified Patankar deferred correction (mPDeC) method removes this restriction, offering high-order accuracy, conservation, and unconditional positivity. However, its solution-dependent Patankar weights make the time update nonlinear, so, unlike with RK methods, preserving (steady and moving) equilibria, i.e., well-balancing (WB), is no longer straightforward. In this paper, we construct high-order, WB, positivity-preserving mPDeC schemes by combining mPDeC with a flux-globalization approach. We demonstrate the idea on the one-dimensional shallow water equations, using a WB A-WENO spatial discretization, and introduce a modified local characteristic decomposition that remains stable in the presence of dry states. Numerical experiments on one-dimensional benchmarks confirm that the method satisfies the desired properties.

title: Extended strange metal and superconductivity in partially filled moiré Hubbard bands
summary: Moiré semiconductors provide a physical realization of the Hubbard model. Bandwidth-tuned Mott transitions and complex phase diagrams mimicking those of high-temperature superconductors have been demonstrated near a weak Mott insulating state at half-band-filling. The platform also provides an opportunity to explore the physics of a partially filled Hubbard band at doping densities far away from the Mott insulator, a regime that has remained largely unexplored. Here we report the emergence of an extended strange metal (ESM), in both doping density and twist angle, in a partially filled Hubbard band of twisted bilayer WSe2. The ESM is in the clean limit, persists down to 100mK, and spans over multiple symmetry-breaking ground states; it also appears only at small twist angles, where electronic correlations are strong. These observations distinguish the state from the reported strange metals associated with quantum criticality and favor the viewpoint that it is an intrinsic state of matter. We also report the observation of a new superconducting dome being developed from the ESM but far away from both the Mott insulating state and the van Hove singularity of the material. Our work opens the door to exploring the new regime of partially filled Hubbard bands in the clean limit.

title: A Hybridizable Discontinuous Galerkin Method for Time-Modulated Drude--Lorentz Media
summary: We formulate and analyze a hybridizable discontinuous Galerkin (HDG) method for Maxwell's equations coupled to four time-modulated Drude--Lorentz models: modulated in-coupling, modulated polarization density, modulated current density, and modulated effective mass. The use of electric displacement and model-dependent continuous material states gives a common treatment of temporal interfaces while preserving the distinct physical transmission rules. We derive energy and stability estimates, establish spatial and event-aligned time-error bounds, and separate time-integration error from error caused by misplaced switching times. Numerical experiments in three dimensions and in reduced modal systems confirm the predicted spatial, temporal, and switch-timing behavior, including the field-jump effect specific to the polarization-density model.

title: Parafermions in polarized $ν=2/3$ Fractional Quantum (Anomalous) Hall Heterostructures
summary: Motivated by recent experimental signatures of fractional Chern insulators in 2D quantum materials, we investigate the realization of $\mathbb Z_3$ parafermion zero modes (PZMs) on edges of spin-polarized $ν=2/3$ fractional quantum Hall states which are proximitized by superconductors. Unlike the spin-unpolarized Halperin state, the polarized $ν=2/3$ edge contains counterpropagating electron and fractional quasihole modes, giving rise to a plethora of competing tunneling and pairing processes. We focus on the vicinity of the fixed point where these modes reorganize into decoupled charge and neutral sectors, with the neutral sector describing an emergent dipole degree of freedom. Using bosonization and renormalization group analysis, we lay out the parameter space in which the interedge dipole interactions gap the neutral sector to stabilize one dominant tunneling and one dominant pairing channel resulting in a double sine-Gordon model in the charge sector which supports $\mathbb{Z}_3$ PZMs at domain walls. We discuss both clean and disordered systems. In clean systems this mechanism requires a certain degree of control of the interaction strength and range. In contrast, disorder can provide a more generic route: While short-ranged, edge-uncorrelated disorder % on the two edges suppresses the simultaneous pinning required for stable parafermion modes, when the disorder on the two edges is sufficiently correlated, as expected for smooth disorder potentials, the parameter regime hosting PZMs increases.

title: Finite Volume Convergence for a Heat Equation with a Measure-Valued Source
summary: Past work with Tom Seidman analyzed the spatial convergence order of the numerical finite element method applied to time-dependent diffusion-reaction equations with a measure-valued source term. For smooth source terms, the numerical method has second-order accuracy, but the non-smooth source terms introduce a limitation of the order that depends on the spatial dimension. This work in honor of Tom extends the analysis to the finite volume method in its clas- sical two-point flux form and shows that the regularity of the source term reduces the convergence order to 1 in two and 0.5 in three spatial dimensions which is reduced from the nominal second-order and depends on the space dimension. Computational tests with a point source modeled by a Dirac delta distribution exhibit the behavior predicted by the analytical results.

title: The ReLU Matrix Decomposition: NP-Hardness, Ill-Posedness, and ReLU-Rank
summary: The ReLU Matrix Decomposition (RMD) approximates a sparse, nonnegative m-by-n matrix X by max(0, WH), where W is an m-by-r matrix, H is an r-by-n matrix, and r is the rank of the decomposition. The most common formulation, referred to as Fro-RMD, minimizes the Frobenius norm of X - max(0, WH) over W and H. We prove that Fro-RMD is NP-hard, even for binary matrices and r = 1; to the best of our knowledge, this is the first complexity result for RMD. We also show that Fro-RMD is ill-posed, in the sense that its infimum may not be attained. We then turn to exact RMD, that is, X = max(0, WH), and define the ReLU-rank of X as the smallest r for which such a decomposition exists. We interpret exact RMDs geometrically as configurations of points and hyperplanes in an r-dimensional space, associated with the rows of W and the columns of H, respectively. Building on this interpretation, we derive upper bounds on the ReLU-rank of diagonal, block-diagonal, and block-sparse matrices and, under an additional structural assumption, improve the best known bound for block-diagonal matrices. Finally, we propose two formulations of exact RMD as feasibility problems: a nonconvex quadratically constrained program, which can be tackled by global solvers such as Gurobi, and a formulation based on the latent model of Saul, (``A nonlinear matrix decomposition for mining the zeros of sparse data', SIMODS, 2022), which we tackle using alternating projections for which we establish local convergence together with asymptotic convergence rates. We compare these two approaches on some numerical examples.

title: Real-Arithmetic Sketched Eigensolvers for Symmetric Matrices
summary: In this work, we develop sketched variants of subspace iteration and TraceMIN, called sSI and sTraceMIN, for real symmetric eigenvalue problems by combining basis whitening with the sketched Rayleigh-Ritz (sRR) procedure. The nonsymmetric projected matrix in sRR may have nonreal eigenpairs, leading to complex arithmetic and additional computational costs. We overcome this difficulty using a real Schur formulation of sRR that keeps the iterations in real arithmetic. We further develop procedures for characteristic subspace selection and convergence monitoring within this formulation. On the theoretical side, we discuss suitable subspace embedding assumptions for sketched eigensolvers that use a fixed sketching matrix throughout the iterations. Under a mild embedding assumption, we establish local convergence results for sSI and sTraceMIN. Numerical experiments demonstrate runtime savings of up to 39% for sSI and 21% for sTraceMIN relative to their standard counterparts on the test problems.
